params_note: dense model (all parameters active); checkpoint total includes vision tower + MTP head, text-only weights loaded by the adapter = 0.75 B
weights_gb_note: decimal GB of the weights as loaded by the adapter (text-only); download_gb is the checkpoint size on the hub (1.75 GB, sum of safetensors files); 4bit = NF4 + double-quant estimate: 0.498 B quantisable linear params x 0.5159 B + remaining params in bf16 (estimate only; bitsandbytes loading not tested here)
fits_single_80gb_detail: bf16: yes (1.5 GB of weights loaded = 1.4 GiB of ~79.7 GiB usable on an 80 GB card, ~77 GiB left for KV cache + activations; core KV formula 48 KiB/token). sbx batching (budgets: 0.37 x free for KV, 14000 prompt tokens, cap 64) then runs ~46 concurrent sequences at 300-token prompts + max_new=400. 4-bit would fit ~0.8 GB but is slower per token and changes the activations the directions are built from - not recommended. Scope: this is the GENERATION path (Ctx.gen / Ctx.run); direction building (Ctx.hidden_last / neutral_stats) has its own budget, see direction_building_memory.

direction_building_memory.applies_to: sbx.core.Ctx.hidden_last and Ctx.neutral_stats (every sbx.dirs recipe). Both run ONE full forward over the whole prompt with output_hidden_states=True and without logits_to_keep, so all num_layers+1 hidden-state tensors AND the logits of every prompt position are alive at once. Generation (Ctx.gen / Ctx.run) is not affected: generate() forces logits_to_keep=1 and keeps no hidden states.
direction_building_memory.formula: bytes per prompt token = (num_layers + 1) * hidden_size * 2 + vocab_size * 2 (bf16 hidden states and logits). A lower bound: attention / MLP transients come on top. sbx batching caps a hidden_last batch at 14000 prompt tokens.
direction_building_memory.free_gb_basis: 79.7 GiB usable on an 80 GB card (as in fits_single_80gb_detail) minus weights_gb_bf16, decimal GB

longest_pool_prompt.basis: evals.get_pool() (wmdp + hard + nonbio: 1174 questions on 2026-11-22, after the evals MAX_PROMPT_CHARS=7500 filter), this key's tokenizer and adapter.build, framings N and E

longest_unfiltered_hard_prompt.basis: data/hard/*.jsonl as read before the evals filter (968 questions, framing E); this question is no longer in any pool, the raw file still has it

Replace with the mean generated length from the first GPU run: np.percentile([ctx.ntok(t) for t in res.texts], [50, 90, 99]).
est_runtime_note: ESTIMATE, not measured: 400 decode steps x ~20 ms/step (HF eager generate on one H100, overhead-bound) = ~8 s per batch of ~46 sequences (batch run to max_new because some sequence usually loops/truncates) => ~0.17 s/question => ~3 min per 1000 questions at 300-token prompts. Without flash-linear-attention + causal-conv1d expect several times slower.
template_notes:
(1) ChatML like Qwen3 (<|im_start|>/<|im_end|>, no BOS; first token id 248045), framing text in the system turn. The template trims message content (leading/trailing whitespace) and raises on a system message that is not first. The /think and /nothink soft switches of Qwen3 are NOT supported (model card); only enable_thinking. (2) The two checkpoints ship DIFFERENT template defaults: Qwen3.5-0.8B renders '<think>

</think>

' unless enable_thinking=True (non-thinking by default, model card), Qwen3.5-9B renders '<think>
' unless enable_thinking=False (thinking by default, model card). The adapter ALWAYS passes enable_thinking explicitly, so behaviour does not depend on the default. (3) Tokenizer/template rendering gives identical prompt strings and token ids under transformers 4.57.6 and 5.2.0 (verified), so offline tests on the old stack are representative. (4) thinking=off: enable_thinking=False => prompts end '<|im_start|>assistant
<think>

</think>

' (activation read point = the '

' after '</think>'); answer_mode 'cot' exactly as for qwen3-*: split() -> ('', visible text), parse_letter() = last 'Answer: X' line (cut turns carry the marker <|sbx_cut|> and are read from an 'Answer:' line only), as for qwen3-*.
known_issues: Greedy decoding (vendor suggests T=0.7/top-p 0.8 for non-thinking Qwen3); repetition is rare at this length but possible.

max_new=400 cap: a visible CoT that is cut at 400 tokens (no end-of-turn token in the decoded text) is unparsed (counted wrong) unless it already wrote an 'Answer:' line: split() appends <|sbx_cut|> to its final text (the visible text is kept for the mention regexes) and parse_letter then reads only an 'Answer:' line, so a letter is never quoted from the middle of unfinished reasoning. Check parse_rate; if >5% are unparsed raise max_new to 512-600.
No separate reasoning channel: m_instr / m_conseq mention regexes scan the whole visible output (CoT + answer).

Instruction-following of 'finish with Answer: <letter>' is not guaranteed under steering. parse_letter reads, in this order: the LAST line that starts with 'Answer:' / 'Final answer:' (a remark after it, e.g. '(Note: the correct answer is B)' under instructed sandbagging, never overrides it), then - turns that ended on their own only - the last in-line statement ('the correct answer is **B**', \boxed{B}; never across a newline, 'if the answer is C, ...' and 'Answer choice D is ...' are skipped), then a last line that is only a label. There is no first-token fallback, so format drift and truncation show up as parse_rate loss rather than as spurious letters. Deliberately not read: 'The correct answer (B) is ...', 'Answer B', "I'd answer B" (no connector after 'answer').
Qwen3.5-0.8B's own default is thinking OFF: this key is the vendor-default behaviour of the model.

REQUIRES transformers>=5.2.0 (first release containing models/qwen3_5; absent in 5.0.0/5.1.0, and the local 4.57.6 stack rejects model_type 'qwen3_5' with ValueError) plus python>=3.10 and torch>=2.4 (transformers 5.x metadata). The local py3.9/torch2.2 environment cannot load or instantiate this model: only tokenizer/template rendering is testable there. load() raises a clear RuntimeError on older transformers.

Loading path: AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(repo) -> Qwen3_5ForCausalLM (text-only; the vision tower and the MTP head are not instantiated, 'mtp.*' / 'model.visual.*' are ignored on load) - verified on a tiny random composite checkpoint round-trip with transformers 5.2.0 and 5.24.0 (logits identical to the full model); the real checkpoint's tensor names (from model.safetensors.index.json) match the text-only model's parameters exactly (see layer_path_verified.checkpoint_key_check). AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(<composite config>) FAILS in 5.2.0 (AttributeError: no vocab_size); pass the text_config. Layer hooks verified on this path (layers at model.model.layers; a Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration keeps them at model.model.language_model.layers - the adapter's layers() handles both).

Hybrid architecture: 3 Gated-DeltaNet (linear attention) layers per full-attention layer. Without the optional kernels (flash-linear-attention, causal-conv1d) transformers falls back to a slow pure-PyTorch implementation (it logs a warning): expect much lower prefill/decode throughput; install both on the pod. Left-padded batches were checked on a tiny random model (last-position states equal the unpadded ones up to bf16 noise; exact through the linear-attention layers).

The repos ship NO generation_config.json: transformers then takes eos_token_id=248044 (<|endoftext|>) from config.json and would NOT stop at <|im_end|> (248046), the token that closes an assistant turn. load() therefore adds <|im_end|> to model.generation_config.eos_token_id (verified on the tiny checkpoint: [248044, 248046]). Without that every sequence could run to max_new.

core.kv_bytes_per_token counts ALL layers, but only the full-attention layers keep a KV cache (linear-attention layers keep a constant-size recurrent state): sbx's batch sizing over-estimates KV memory by ~4x for this family (conservative: smaller batches than necessary). See kv_bytes_per_token_true.

No prior sbx evidence for this architecture: 3 of 4 layers are linear-attention (Gated DeltaNet) layers. The residual-stream conventions (1-based layer index, hook on the layer output, read at the last prompt token) are unchanged and were verified, but whether directions and interventions behave as in dense transformers is untested.
Framing.effort has no meaning for this family: render() warns (UserWarning) if a framing sets it and otherwise ignores it.
recommended_gpu: any GPU >= 8GB (or CPU for smoke tests); this is the tiny test target - 'cot' keys run in seconds.
greedy_only_note: sbx decodes greedily (do_sample=False); vendor-recommended sampling settings are not used.
thinking_switch: chat-template kwarg enable_thinking=True/False (always passed explicitly by the adapter)
